message.content:
**Columbia University** is a private Ivy League research university located in New York City, United States. It was founded in 1754 as King's College and was renamed Columbia College in 1784, then Columbia University in 1896. Here are some key points: | Topic | Details | |-------|---------| | **Location** | Morningside Heights, Manhattan, New York City (main campus). Additional campuses include the Columbia Business School in Midtown Manhattan, the Columbia School of the Arts in Brooklyn, and the Columbia Center for the Performing Arts in Upper Manhattan. | | **Founding** | 1754 (King's College) – the first institution of higher education in the American colonies. | | **Academic Structure** | • Undergraduate College (Columbia College)
• Graduate and professional schools: Columbia Law School, Columbia Business School, Columbia School of Engineering and Applied Science, Columbia School of Architecture, Columbia School of Journalism, Columbia School of International and Public Affairs, Columbia School of Nursing, Columbia School of Social Work, etc. | | **Student Body** | Roughly 30,000 students (≈ 8,000 undergraduates, 22,000 graduate & professional). | | **Faculty** | About 2,000 faculty members, many of whom are Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and other distinguished scholars. | | **Research** | One of the world’s leading research universities, with strengths in fields such as physics, chemistry, biology, economics, political science, literature, and computer science. It hosts numerous research centers and institutes (e.g., Columbia Climate Institute, Columbia Center for the Study of Social Issues). | | **Notable Alumni** | Presidents (e.g., Theodore Roosevelt, Franklin D. Roosevelt), Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, CEOs, artists, and scholars. | | **Campus Highlights** | • Low Memorial Library (iconic central building)
• Morningside Park
• The Columbia University Medical Center (NYU‑Columbia)
• The Pulitzer Prize-winning Columbia Journalism School’s building | | **Rankings** | Consistently ranked among the top universities worldwide (e.g., QS World University Rankings, U.S. News & World Report). | | **Admissions** | Highly selective; acceptance rate typically below 5%. | If you need more specific information—such as current enrollment numbers, tuition, or details about a particular program—just let me know!
